The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch
Cited in the Divine Council Index entry on Matthew 17:1-8.

abel.title: Abel
abel.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
abel.note: Adam and Eve's second son, and a shepherd. God took his offering, the firstborn of the flock, and passed over his brother Cain's, and that is where the first murder comes from. Hebrews says it was the faith behind the offering, not the offering itself.

abia-2.title: Abia
abia-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
abia-2.note: Matthew's spelling of Abijah, the king of Judah, sitting in the genealogy. One verse, one name in a chain.

abiud.title: Abiud
abiud.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
abiud.note: Matthew's genealogy puts him between Zerubbabel and Joseph. Luke's version of the list does not have him, and nothing else about him is recorded.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

achaz.title: Achaz
achaz.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
achaz.note: Matthew's genealogy spells Ahaz this way. He is in the list as an ancestor of Jesus, and that is the whole of his appearance here.

achim.title: Achim
achim.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
achim.note: Matthew's genealogy has him between Zadok and Eliud. Nothing else anywhere mentions him.

alpheus.title: Alpheus
alpheus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
alpheus.note: Father of the apostle James, which is how that James is told apart from James the son of Zebedee.

aminadab.title: Aminadab
aminadab.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aminadab.note: Amminadab in its Greek form. Matthew and Luke both name him as David's ancestor through Judah, and his daughter Elisheba married Aaron, so the one family runs into the priests and the kings.

amon.title: Amon
amon.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amon.note: The son of Manasseh. He followed his father's early idolatry and never turned back, and his own officials killed him after two years. The people executed the plotters and made his young son Josiah king.

andrew.title: Andrew
andrew.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
andrew.note: Peter's brother, and in John's Gospel a disciple of John the Baptist first, who followed Jesus and straight away brought Peter to meet him. He keeps turning up at practical moments: the boy with five loaves and two fish, the Greeks who came asking for Jesus. Tradition says he was crucified on an X-shaped cross.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

archelaus.title: Archelaus
archelaus.about: Ethnarch living at the time of the New Testament
archelaus.note: Herod the Great's son. He inherited Judea, Samaria and Idumea and ruled them as ethnarch, harshly enough that his own subjects sent a delegation to Rome against him, and Augustus deposed him and exiled him to Gaul. Joseph settled in Galilee coming back from Egypt because Archelaus was reigning in Judea.

arimathaea.title: Arimathaea
arimathaea.note: Joseph's town. He was the rich, secret disciple who asked Pilate for Jesus' body and laid it in his own new tomb, and all four Gospels name him by this place. Where it was is uncertain, and many scholars put it at Ramathaim-zophim, a few miles northwest of Jerusalem.

asa.title: Asa
asa.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asa.note: King of Judah for forty-one years, and a real reformer. He removed his own grandmother as queen mother over an obscene idol and drove the male shrine prostitutes out. Early on he trusted God against a huge Cushite invasion, but late in life he hired a foreign king against northern Israel instead.

azor.title: Azor
azor.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
azor.note: In Matthew's genealogy of Jesus he sits between Eliakim and Zadok, one link in the chain from Zerubbabel down to Joseph. Nothing else about him is recorded.

babylon.title: Babylon
babylon.note: The Mesopotamian empire that destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in 586 BC and carried Judah off. Later Scripture, Revelation included, uses its name as shorthand for worldly power.

baptist.title: Baptist
baptist.note: John, son of the priest Zechariah and Elizabeth. He was born to elderly parents after an angel said he would be. He preached in the wilderness.

bar-jona.title: Bar-jona
bar-jona.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
bar-jona.note: Son of Jonah. Jesus calls Simon Peter this right after Peter says Jesus is the Christ, and it names Peter's father as a man called Jonah or John.

barabbas.title: Barabbas
barabbas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
barabbas.note: Held for insurrection and murder. Under a Passover custom Pilate offered the crowd one prisoner, Barabbas or Jesus. They chose Barabbas, and Jesus was crucified.

barachias.title: Barachias
barachias.about: High Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
barachias.note: Matthew 23:35 names him as father of the Zacharias murdered between the temple and the altar. The wording fits Zechariah the priest stoned in the temple court under King Joash.

bartholomeus.title: Bartholomeus
bartholomeus.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
bartholomeus.note: One of the twelve. Many take him for Nathanael, since the Synoptic Gospels never mention a Nathanael and John's Gospel never mentions a Bartholomew.

beelzebub.title: Beelzebub
beelzebub.about: An angel in the Old Testament
beelzebub.note: Lord of the flies. It started as a title for a Philistine god and became a common New Testament name for the prince of demons. Jesus's opponents said he cast out demons by Beelzebub's power.

bethany.title: Bethany
bethany.note: Two places in the Gospels carry this name. The better known is a village on the southeastern slope of the Mount of Olives, about two miles from Jerusalem, where Lazarus, Mary and Martha lived. Jesus stayed there in his final days.

bethlehem.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem.note: House of bread. It is a small town about five miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Ephrath, where Rachel died and was buried and where Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields. David was born there and anointed there.

bethphage.title: Bethphage
bethphage.note: They found the donkey here. Jesus sent two disciples ahead to this village on the Mount of Olives, near Bethany, to fetch the animal he rode into Jerusalem. The name means house of unripe figs.

bethsaida.title: Bethsaida
bethsaida.note: A fishing town on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee, home to Peter, Andrew and Philip. Jesus rebuked it more sharply than any of the Galilean towns that would not repent.

boaz.title: Boaz
boaz.note: A wealthy landowner in Bethlehem, related to Naomi's dead husband Elimelech. He noticed Ruth, the widowed Moabite, gleaning behind his harvesters, and he agreed to act as kinsman-redeemer.

caesar.title: Caesar
caesar.about: Emperor living at the time of the New Testament
caesar.note: Not one man. Caesar is the New Testament's title for whoever was Roman emperor, Augustus when Jesus was born and Tiberius when he was crucified.

caesarea.title: Caesarea
caesarea.note: Herod the Great built it as a Roman port on the Mediterranean coast, and it served as the administrative capital of Roman Judea. Cornelius the centurion lived there. Paul spent two years there in prison.

caiaphas.title: Caiaphas
caiaphas.about: High Priest living at the time of the New Testament
caiaphas.note: The high priest who presided over the council that condemned Jesus. Beforehand he argued it was better for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to suffer, and John's Gospel reads those words as more than he knew.

cananaean.title: Cananaean
cananaean.about: Political group in the New Testament
cananaean.note: Simon's byname in the lists of the Twelve, in Matthew 10:4 and Mark 3:18. Older translations render it Canaanite, but it has nothing to do with Canaan.

capernaum.title: Capernaum
capernaum.note: Jesus left Nazareth and made this fishing town on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee his base, and it is called his own city. Several of his best known miracles and teachings happened there.

chorazin.title: Chorazin
chorazin.note: Jesus did many of his miracles in this Galilee town and then pronounced a woe on it, alongside Bethsaida and Capernaum, because it did not repent. It is identified with Khirbet Karazeh about two miles north of Capernaum, where a black basalt synagogue has been dug up.

christ.title: Christ
christ.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
christ.note: A title, not a surname. It is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one, and the New Testament gives it to Jesus of Nazareth as the king, priest and deliverer the Old Testament promised. His life and ministry are under Jesus.

daniel.title: Daniel
daniel.about: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
daniel.note: Carried off to Babylon as a young noble of Judah and renamed by his captors, he rose to high office under three empires without giving up his faith. That refusal got him a night in the lions' den. The visions he received run to the book's last chapter.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

decapolis.title: Decapolis
decapolis.note: The name is Greek for ten cities, a loose league of Hellenistic towns mostly east and southeast of the Sea of Galilee, Gerasa and Philadelphia among them. Crowds from there followed Jesus. The man freed from Legion near Gerasa went round the whole Decapolis telling what had happened to him.

easter.title: Easter
easter.note: The King James has Easter once, at Acts 12:4, and the Greek word underneath it is pascha, Passover. Every later translation says so.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

eleazar-7.title: Eleazar
eleazar-7.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
eleazar-7.note: A man from the exile and the return, and Matthew is the only book that names him.

eli-2.title: Eli
eli-2.note: The Aramaic cry from the cross, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani. Matthew keeps the words untranslated and then renders them.

eliakim-3.title: Eliakim
eliakim-3.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
eliakim-3.note: One of 4 men called Eliakim. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Matthew.

elijah.title: Elijah
elijah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elijah.note: A prophet from Tishbe in Gilead who took on Ahab and Jezebel over Baal worship and beat 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel with fire from heaven. Straight after, he ran into the wilderness sure he was the last faithful man left, and God met him in a quiet voice, not in wind or earthquake or fire. He did not die; a whirlwind took him up while Elisha watched.

eliud.title: Eliud
eliud.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
eliud.note: Son of Achim and father of Eleazar in Matthew's genealogy, several generations before Joseph. Outside that list he is unknown.

emmanuel.title: Emmanuel
emmanuel.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
emmanuel.note: God with us. Matthew quotes Isaiah 7:14 and gives the name to Jesus at his birth, more as a title than what anyone called him day to day.

esrom.title: Esrom
esrom.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
esrom.note: Hezron, in the Greek form. He was Judah's grandson through Perez and is in both Matthew's and Luke's genealogies of Jesus.

ezekias.title: Ezekias
ezekias.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ezekias.note: Hezekiah, in the Greek of Matthew's genealogy. He was the reforming king of Judah who outlasted Sennacherib's siege in 701 BC, and Sennacherib's Prism boasts of shutting him up like a bird in a cage without claiming the city.

gadarene.title: Gadarene
gadarene.note: Matthew sets the healing here, in the country around Gadara, one of the Decapolis cities east of the Sea of Galilee, where the spirits went into a herd of pigs. Other manuscripts and the parallels read Gerasene or Gergesene. Gadara itself is Umm Qais in Jordan now, with its Roman ruins dug out.

galilee.title: Galilee
galilee.note: Jesus grew up here and did most of his public work around the Sea of Galilee. Judeans thought the north provincial and mixed, which is the edge on Nathanael's question about whether anything good could come out of Nazareth.

gennesaret.title: Gennesaret
gennesaret.note: The fertile plain on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee, and by extension the lake itself, which the Old Testament calls Chinnereth. Josephus said almost every kind of tree and crop grew there most of the year. In 1986 a first-century fishing boat came out of the mud near Kibbutz Ginosar on that shore.

gethsemane.title: Gethsemane
gethsemane.note: An olive grove at the foot of the Mount of Olives, across the Kidron Valley from Jerusalem, where Jesus often went with his disciples and where he prayed in anguish the night he was arrested. The garden has been honoured roughly there since at least the fourth century. The olive trees standing now date to the medieval period.

golgotha.title: Golgotha
golgotha.note: The name is Aramaic for place of a skull, Calvary in Latin, where Jesus was crucified outside Jerusalem's walls. The Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Garden Tomb both have their advocates, and neither can be confirmed.

gomorrha.title: Gomorrha
gomorrha.note: The Greek spelling, used in the New Testament. Jesus says it will go easier for Sodom and Gomorrha than for a town that turns his messengers away, and Peter and Jude both point to it as proof that God punishes the ungodly.

herod-2.title: Herod
herod-2.note: King when Jesus was born. When the magi did not come back to him, Herod the Great ordered the boys of Bethlehem killed. He also enlarged the Jerusalem temple, and Josephus tells his story at length.

herod.title: Herod
herod.about: Tetrarch living at the time of the New Testament
herod.note: Herod Antipas, the son of Herod the Great. He ruled Galilee through Jesus's ministry and beheaded John the Baptist for condemning his marriage, and Luke has him mock Jesus before the crucifixion.

herodians.title: Herodians
herodians.about: Political group in the New Testament
herodians.note: Partisans of Herod, in the plainest sense of the name. They backed Herod's dynasty and Roman rule, and still joined the Pharisees, whose views they did not share, to try to trap Jesus over paying taxes to Caesar.

herodias.title: Herodias
herodias.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
herodias.note: Granddaughter of Herod the Great. She left her first husband for his half-brother, Herod Antipas, and when John the Baptist called the marriage unlawful she had her daughter dance at a banquet and ask for his head. Josephus gives a different reason for John's death, a political execution.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

isaiah.title: Isaiah
isaiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
isaiah.note: Amoz's son, a prophet in Jerusalem in the eighth century, who counselled four kings of Judah and is quoted in the New Testament more than any other prophet. He gave his two sons names that were sermons, Shear-jashub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem he told Hezekiah the city would stand, and the Taylor Prism brags of the siege without ever claiming the city fell.

iscariot.title: Iscariot
iscariot.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
iscariot.note: Judas Iscariot kept the money for the twelve, and John says he stole from it. He sold Jesus for thirty pieces of silver and picked him out with a kiss in Gethsemane. Afterwards he gave the money back and hanged himself, though Matthew and Acts tell his death differently.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jacob-3.title: Jacob
jacob-3.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
jacob-3.note: Matthew names him twice, and he is a man from the exile and the return.

jacob-2.title: Jacob
jacob-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob-2.note: In the New Testament the name mostly means the patriarch, set beside Abraham and Isaac, and Luke's angel promises Mary that Jesus will reign "over the house of Jacob forever". Matthew's genealogy also has a Jacob as the father of Joseph.

james.title: James
james.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
james.note: Zebedee's son and John's older brother. He was one of the three closest to Jesus, and the first of the twelve to be killed, by Herod Agrippa the First.

james-3.title: James
james-3.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
james-3.note: Alphaeus's son, one of the twelve, and the Gospels say almost nothing else about him.

james-2.title: James
james-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
james-2.note: The brother of Jesus. He did not believe during the ministry, then led the Jerusalem church after the resurrection, and the letter of James is traditionally his.

jechonias.title: Jechonias
jechonias.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jechonias.note: The Greek form of Jeconiah, the king of Judah taken to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar after three months on the throne. Matthew's genealogy turns on him at the exile. Babylonian ration tablets list food for "Yaukin, king of the land of Yahud" and his sons.

jeremiah.title: Jeremiah
jeremiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeremiah.note: A priest's son from Anathoth, called as a young man in Josiah's thirteenth year. For four decades he told Judah Babylon was coming, and for that he was jailed, dropped in a cistern, and had his scroll burned. He saw Jerusalem fall as he had said, then was dragged off to Egypt against his will. His scribe Baruch may be the Berekhyahu on a clay seal from his lifetime.

jericho.title: Jericho
jericho.note: Israel crossed the Jordan and Jericho was the first city it took, walled and gated, with its own king. Achan died for what he stole from the plunder there, a Babylonian robe and silver that belonged to God. By then the place was already ancient: digging at the site has turned up remains about ten thousand years old.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

jesus.title: Jesus
jesus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jesus.note: Born in Bethlehem to Mary and raised in Nazareth in Galilee. Around thirty he began teaching in parables, healing, and gathering twelve disciples, until he was arrested in Jerusalem at Passover, tried before the council and Pontius Pilate, and crucified. His followers said he rose bodily three days later, and the New Testament names him the Messiah, God's own Son become human.

joatham.title: Joatham
joatham.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joatham.note: Matthew's spelling of Jotham, king of Judah, who stands in the genealogy between his father Uzziah and his son Ahaz. He strengthened Jerusalem's defences and brought the Ammonites under.

john-2.title: John
john-2.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
john-2.note: Zebedee's son and James's younger brother, a fisherman, and with Peter and James one of the three who saw what the rest did not, the transfiguration and Gethsemane among it. From the cross Jesus gave him his mother Mary to look after. Tradition makes him the disciple Jesus loved and credits him with the fourth Gospel, three letters, and Revelation, written in exile on Patmos.

john.title: John
john.about: Prophet living at the time of the New Testament
john.note: The prophet who comes out of the wilderness in Matthew 3, preaching repentance and baptising. Jesus came to him to be baptised. Later, from prison, he sent his own disciples to ask whether Jesus was the one.

jonah.title: Jonah
jonah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jonah.note: God told him to preach to Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, Israel's enemy, and he took a ship the other way. A storm, three days in a great fish, and then he did preach, and the whole city repented and God spared it. That made Jonah furious. The book stops with God questioning his anger and leaves it there.

joram.title: Joram
joram.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joram.note: Another form of Jehoram, and the kings of Israel and Judah called by it are covered under that entry.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

josaphat.title: Josaphat
josaphat.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
josaphat.note: Jehoshaphat, in the Greek spelling Matthew uses in the genealogy of Jesus. He was the king of Judah known for his reforms and his uneasy alliance with the northern kingdom.

joseph-3.title: Joseph
joseph-3.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
joseph-3.note: He asked for Jesus's body after the crucifixion, wrapped it, and laid it in a tomb, and every gospel account has him doing it.

joseph-2.title: Joseph
joseph-2.about: Mary's husband living at the time of the New Testament
joseph-2.note: A descendant of David from Nazareth, engaged to Mary when she turned out to be pregnant. An angel in a dream talked him out of quietly ending it, and he raised Jesus as his legal father. Scripture says nothing of him after Jesus's boyhood.

josias.title: Josias
josias.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
josias.note: Matthew's Greek spelling of Josiah, the boy king of Judah who launched a reform after a scroll of the law turned up during temple repairs, and who died in battle against Pharaoh Necho.

judaea.title: Judaea
judaea.note: The Roman name for the southern part of the land around Jerusalem, roughly old Judah. Client kings of Herod's family ruled it, then Roman procurators like Pontius Pilate. John the Baptist preached in its wilderness and the Passion happened there. After the revolt of AD 66 to 70 Rome struck coins reading "Judaea Capta."

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

magdala.title: Magdala
magdala.note: The home town that gave Mary Magdalene her name, on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee. Matthew says Jesus went to the region of Magdala after feeding the four thousand, where Mark calls the same area Dalmanutha. Digging there since 2009 has turned up a first-century synagogue and the carved Magdala Stone, one of the earliest pictures of the Temple's menorah.

magdalene.title: Magdalene
magdalene.note: It means "from Magdala," the town on the Sea of Galilee, and it keeps this Mary apart from the other Marys in the Gospels. She watched the crucifixion and was the first to see the risen Jesus. The old idea that she was the sinful woman of Luke 7 has nothing in the text behind it.

manasses.title: Manasses
manasses.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
manasses.note: The Greek form of Manasseh. Matthew uses it for the king of Judah in Jesus' family line, the one who reigned longest and led the nation into idols.

mary.title: Mary
mary.about: Jesus' mother living at the time of the New Testament
mary.note: Jesus' mother. She was engaged to Joseph when Gabriel told her she would bear the Messiah, she raised Jesus in Nazareth, and she stood at the cross when he died.

mary-3.title: Mary
mary-3.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
mary-3.note: Another Mary in the Gospels, one of the women at the cross and at the empty tomb, and not to be mixed up with Jesus' mother or the Mary of Bethany.

master.title: Master
master.note: A title, not a name. Luke especially uses it for Jesus where the others would say teacher.

matthan.title: Matthan
matthan.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
matthan.note: Matthew's genealogy makes him Jacob's father and grandfather to Joseph, Mary's husband. Luke gives Joseph a different grandfather, Matthat, one of the places the two lines part, probably because they trace different lines of descent.

matthew.title: Matthew
matthew.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
matthew.note: A tax collector, which made him an outcast among fellow Jews for working on Rome's behalf, until Jesus called him straight from his booth to be one of the twelve. Mark and Luke call him Levi. He threw a big dinner for Jesus with other tax collectors, and early church tradition says he wrote the Gospel that carries his name, aimed at Jewish readers.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

naasson.title: Naasson
naasson.note: The Greek spelling of Nahshon, prince of Judah in the wilderness and brother-in-law to Aaron through his sister Elisheba. Matthew and Luke both list him among Jesus' ancestors.

nazarene.title: Nazarene
nazarene.note: It means from Nazareth, Jesus' home town, and it became the name for his followers too, "the sect of the Nazarenes" in Acts 24:5. Matthew ties it to prophecy, possibly playing on the Hebrew word for "branch" in Isaiah 11. Arabic and Hebrew still call Christians by it.

nazareth.title: Nazareth
nazareth.note: A small village in the hills of Galilee, never named in the Old Testament and not thought much of, which is likely the edge on Nathanael's question about whether anything good could come from it. Gabriel came to Mary there, and Jesus grew up there. When he preached in its synagogue, his neighbours drove him out.

nephthalim.title: Nephthalim
nephthalim.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
nephthalim.note: The Greek spelling of Naphtali. Matthew uses it for the land where a people in darkness see a great light, as Jesus begins his work there.

noah.title: Noah
noah.about: Flood survivor living at the time before the Flood
noah.note: God picked him as the one righteous man of his generation and told him to build an ark. His family came through the flood with him, along with pairs of every kind of animal. Afterward God made a covenant with him.

obed.title: Obed
obed.note: Boaz and Ruth's son, and Naomi helped raise him. He was David's grandfather, which puts Ruth's story inside the royal line.

ozias.title: Ozias
ozias.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ozias.note: Matthew's spelling of Uzziah in the genealogy of Jesus, son of Joram.

peter.title: Peter
peter.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
peter.note: A Galilean fisherman named Simon. Jesus renamed him Cephas, or Peter, which means rock. He became the most prominent of the twelve and the first to confess Jesus as the Messiah.

phares.title: Phares
phares.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
phares.note: Matthew and Luke both list Perez, son of Judah and Tamar, in the genealogy of Jesus under this Greek spelling.

pharisee.title: Pharisee
pharisee.about: Religious group in the New Testament
pharisee.note: A Jewish movement devoted to strict keeping of the law, the written text and a large body of oral tradition around it. They carried real weight in the religious life of the people. They argue with Jesus again and again.

philip.title: Philip
philip.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
philip.note: One of the twelve, from Bethsaida like Peter and Andrew. Philip found Nathanael and brought him to Jesus, and in John's Gospel he gets asked how they were going to feed the crowd.

philip-3.title: Philip
philip-3.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
philip-3.note: One of 4 men called Philip. This one is a man from the New Testament, named twice in Matthew and Mark.

pilate.title: Pilate
pilate.about: Ruler living at the time of the New Testament
pilate.note: Pontius Pilate, Roman governor of Judea. He said three times that he found no guilt in Jesus, and then gave the crowd and the religious leaders what they wanted and had him crucified.

raca.title: Raca
raca.note: A term of contempt, roughly empty-head, which Jesus says is enough to answer for.

rachab.title: Rachab
rachab.note: Matthew's spelling of Rahab, in the genealogy of Jesus, wife of Salmon and mother of Boaz.

rachel.title: Rachel
rachel.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
rachel.note: Jacob's favourite wife. He was tricked into marrying her older sister Leah first and had to work another seven years for Rachel. For years Leah bore son after son while Rachel had none.

rama.title: Rama
rama.note: Matthew quotes Jeremiah's Rachel weeping for her children in Rama, and applies it to Herod killing the baby boys of Bethlehem. Rama is the Greek form of Ramah.

roboam.title: Roboam
roboam.about: King living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy
roboam.note: Matthew's Greek spelling of Rehoboam, Solomon's son, under whom the kingdom split.

ruth.title: Ruth
ruth.note: A Moabite widow who would not leave her mother-in-law Naomi. "Where you go I will go," she said, and went with her to Bethlehem, where she married Naomi's relative Boaz.

sadducee.title: Sadducee
sadducee.about: Religious group in the New Testament
sadducee.note: A party drawn mostly from the priestly aristocracy. They rejected the oral tradition the Pharisees kept, and they denied the resurrection of the body.

sadoc.title: Sadoc
sadoc.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
sadoc.note: In Matthew's genealogy, between Zerubbabel's family and Joseph. Nothing further is recorded.

salathiel.title: Salathiel
salathiel.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
salathiel.note: Son of the exiled king Jeconiah, also called Shealtiel, and in most lines the father of Zerubbabel, who led the return from Babylon.

salmon.title: Salmon
salmon.note: He was Boaz's father, and his wife was Rahab, the woman who hid Israel's spies at Jericho, which puts him in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus.

samaritan.title: Samaritan
samaritan.note: The people who lived in Samaria in Jesus' day. 2 Kings traces them back to the Israelites left behind and the foreigners Assyria brought in. They worshiped at a temple of their own.

satan.title: Satan
satan.about: An angel in the Old Testament
satan.note: The name means adversary. In Job he questions whether Job's goodness is real, and in Zechariah he stands to accuse Joshua the high priest before the angel of the Lord.

sidon.title: Sidon
sidon.note: The older of the two great Phoenician ports, north of Tyre. It was allotted to Asher, but Asher never took it.

simon-4.title: Simon
simon-4.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
simon-4.note: One of the twelve apostles. The title Zealot tells him apart from Simon Peter and probably means he had belonged to a movement opposed to Roman rule. Nothing else about him is recorded.

simon.title: Simon
simon.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
simon.note: Simon Peter, called from his fishing in Matthew 4:18 and named first among the twelve apostles. In Matthew 16:16 he is the one who answers the question.

simon-6.title: Simon
simon-6.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
simon-6.note: The man made to carry the cross on the way to the crucifixion, in Matthew 27:32, Mark 15:21 and Luke 23:26.

simon-7.title: Simon
simon-7.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
simon-7.note: One of 7 men called Simon. This one is a man from the New Testament, named twice in Matthew and Mark.

sion.title: Sion
sion.note: Another spelling of Zion. The hill in Jerusalem came to stand for the whole city, and in poetry for the place where God lives among his people.

sodom.title: Sodom
sodom.note: Sodom was destroyed by fire from heaven along with Gomorrah, and the rest of Scripture keeps pointing back to it as the picture of judgment. It was one of the cities of the plain near the Dead Sea.

solomon.title: Solomon
solomon.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
solomon.note: David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

syria.title: Syria
syria.note: The region northeast of Israel, called Aram in the Old Testament. In the New Testament Antioch was its chief city and the base Paul's journeys started from, and Luke dates Jesus's birth by a census under Quirinius.

thamar.title: Thamar
thamar.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
thamar.note: She is Tamar, in Matthew's spelling: Judah's daughter-in-law, who conceived Perez and Zerah by Judah after he failed to give her his youngest son. She is one of four women in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus.

thomas.title: Thomas
thomas.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
thomas.note: One of the twelve, called the twin. He would not believe Jesus had risen until he could touch the wounds, and when Jesus showed him his hands and side he said, my Lord and my God.

tyre.title: Tyre
tyre.note: The leading Phoenician port, partly on the mainland and partly on an island offshore, rich from sea trade and purple dye made from murex shells. Its king Hiram sent cedar and craftsmen for David and Solomon. The prophets attacked its pride and said it would fall.

urias.title: Urias
urias.about: Bathsheba's husband living at the time of United Monarchy
urias.note: Matthew's genealogy says David fathered Solomon by the wife of Urias. It is Uriah the Hittite, and naming him puts David's sin into the family tree of Jesus.

zabulon.title: Zabulon
zabulon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zabulon.note: The Greek form of Zebulun. Matthew uses it for the country where Jesus started preaching after he left Nazareth for Capernaum, and Revelation counts it among the sealed tribes.

zara.title: Zara
zara.about: Judah's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zara.note: Matthew's spelling of Zerah, Perez's twin, named and passed over because the line runs through Perez.

zebedee.title: Zebedee
zebedee.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
zebedee.note: He fished, and he was the father of James and John. He had hired men working with him, and when his sons left the boat to follow Jesus, he stayed.

zechariah-2.title: Zechariah
zechariah-2.about: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zechariah-2.note: Matthew and Luke name him twice, and he is a priest from the divided-kingdom years.

zerubbabel.title: Zerubbabel
zerubbabel.about: Governor living at the time of Exile and Return
zerubbabel.note: He came from David's line and led the first exiles back from Babylon to Jerusalem. As governor he laid the temple's foundation and, with Haggai and Zechariah pushing, saw it finished.
